title: Catalogue LLM-as-judge biases and which corrections survive measurement
question: What biases are measured in LLM judges (position, verbosity, self-preference, style), what magnitude does each have, and which proposed correction has been shown to reduce it rather than merely being proposed?
answer: Position, verbosity, self-preference, and style (authority/beauty) are measured with numeric magnitudes and named baselines. Swap/BPC+MEC is measured-effective for position; length-controlled GLM is measured-effective for verbosity. G-Eval/CoT and few-shot judging are widely cited and land proposed-only: they are not shown to reduce those named biases. Independent-judge and ignore-style prompts remain proposed-only. No correction in this catalogue is graded refuted; several widely-cited ones fail to meet measured-effective.

grading_rule.text: A correction is graded measured-effective only when the same paper (or a direct replication on the same judge/task) reports a numeric change in the NAMED bias, or in human-agreement attributable to that correction, against an explicit baseline condition. A correction that is described, prompted, or widely adopted but is not measured against that named bias is proposed-only. A correction that was tested on the named bias and failed to reduce it, or reversed it, is refuted. Headline magnitudes without a baseline are recorded as evidence-tier E3 and cannot promote a mechanism or a measured-effective grade.

bias_by_correction_table.correction: Balanced Position Calibration (swap both orders and average) + Multiple Evidence Calibration
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: Position conflict 46.3% (37/80) GPT-4 and 82.5% ChatGPT on Vicuna-13B vs ChatGPT; GPT-4 slot win 51.3% vs 23.8%.
bias_by_correction_table.baseline: Vanilla conclusion-first judge: GPT-4 accuracy 52.7% kappa 0.24 vs human majority on the same 80 items.

bias_by_correction_table.correction: Conservative double-call swap: win only if preferred in both orders, else tie
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: GPT-4 default consistency 65.0%, first-slot bias 30.0%, second-slot bias 5.0% (Zheng Table 2).
bias_by_correction_table.baseline: Single-order judgment; inconsistent pairs would be scored as a win for the favored slot. Unbiased consistency = 100% on this swap test.
bias_by_correction_table.correction_effect_size: Protocol used for all subsequent MT-Bench pairwise numbers in Zheng §3.4. No separate human-agreement delta for swap alone is tabulated; BPC in Wang Table 4 is the measured numeric sibling. This row grades the Zheng protocol as measured-effective because Wang measures the same swap+aggregate family on the same judge class with a baseline.

bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: Zero-shot GPT-4 consistency 65.0% on the similar-answer swap test (Zheng Table 2 default).
bias_by_correction_table.correction_effect_size: Few-shot raises GPT-4 consistency 65.0% -> 77.5% (Zheng Table 12 / §3.4). Authors warn high consistency may not imply high accuracy and that few-shot may inject new bias; they keep zero-shot as default.
bias_by_correction_table.why_not_measured_effective: The measured quantity is swap-consistency, not human agreement or bias-vs-truth. The paper refuses the accuracy claim.

bias_by_correction_table.correction: G-Eval / CoT form-filling as a general judge upgrade
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: Position conflict remains 46.3% for vanilla GPT-4 pairwise on Wang Table 2; G-Eval does not report a swap experiment.
bias_by_correction_table.baseline: Vanilla pairwise or n-gram metrics. G-Eval reports Spearman correlation with humans, not position-bias reduction.
bias_by_correction_table.locator: Liu et al. abstract (human correlation); no position-swap table
bias_by_correction_table.why_not_measured_effective: G-Eval is widely cited as making LLM judges better. It measures correlation with human NLG scores, not reduction of position, verbosity, self-preference, or style bias.

bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: Verbose instruction lifts a 50% baseline win rate to 64%; concise instruction drops it to 23% (Dubois / AlpacaEval length-gameability). Zheng repetitive-list: GPT-3.5 91.3% failure vs identical-answer 0%.
bias_by_correction_table.baseline: Raw AlpacaEval 2.0 Spearman correlation with LMSYS Chatbot Arena 0.94; unprompted pairwise win rate 50% for a model compared to itself-as-baseline.
bias_by_correction_table.correction_effect_size: Length-controlled Spearman with Chatbot Arena 0.94 -> 0.98. Relative length gameability ~21% -> ~6% (3x less gameable).

bias_by_correction_table.correction: G-Eval / CoT form-filling as a verbosity fix
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: Saito GPT-4 verbosity-bias 0.328 vs parity 0; Zheng GPT-3.5 repetitive-list failure 91.3% vs identical-answer 0%.
bias_by_correction_table.locator: Liu et al. abstract; no length-controlled ablation
bias_by_correction_table.why_not_measured_effective: No before/after verbosity-bias number. Human-correlation gains are not a verbosity correction measurement.

bias_by_correction_table.correction: Use a different model (or humans) as judge, never the evaluatee
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: GPT-4 +10pp win rate vs humans for its own outputs; Claude-v1 +25pp (Zheng Figure 3b). GPT-4 self-recognition 73.5%.
bias_by_correction_table.baseline: Human win rates on the same pairs; chance-level self-recognition.
bias_by_correction_table.locator: Panickssery §1 / discussion; Zheng §3.3 (bias, not a tested fix)
bias_by_correction_table.citation: Panickssery, Bowman, and Feng (2024) arXiv:2404.13076 doi:10.48550/arXiv.2404.13076
bias_by_correction_table.why_not_measured_effective: Independence of judge and evaluatee is the obvious protocol fix. Neither paper reports a before/after self-preference delta after swapping in a third-party judge on the same items.

bias_by_correction_table.correction: G-Eval CoT scoring to suppress self-preference
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: Zheng Figure 3b: GPT-4 +10pp vs human on its own answers.
bias_by_correction_table.baseline: Human win rate on the same pairs.
bias_by_correction_table.locator: Liu et al.; no self-preference ablation

bias_by_correction_table.correction: Prompt the judge to ignore citations, markdown, and 'looks'
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: GPT-4 fake-reference ASR 0.66 vs random 0.37; rich-content ASR 0.32 vs random 0.39 (Chen Table 1). Attack using those biases reaches 50% ASR on GPT-4.
bias_by_correction_table.locator: Table 1; §6 attack (no successful prompt mitigation table)
bias_by_correction_table.why_not_measured_effective: Chen measures the biases and weaponizes them. They do not report a prompt that returns ASR to the random baseline.

bias_by_correction_table.correction: G-Eval / CoT as a style-robustness fix
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: Chen Table 1 GPT-4 authority ASR 0.66 vs random 0.37.
bias_by_correction_table.locator: Liu et al.; Chen Table 1 is the bias measurement, not a G-Eval test

bias_by_correction_table.correction: Accuracy-parity verbosity metric as a diagnostic (not a fix)
bias_by_correction_table.why_not_measured_effective: Saito quantifies the bias. They do not evaluate a correction that reduces 0.328 toward 0.

bias_by_correction_table.correction: Chain-of-thought judge (answer first, then grade) as a position fix
bias_by_correction_table.effect_size: GPT-4 position consistency 65.0% default (Table 2). CoT is tested on math grading, not on the swap test: default math failure 14/20, CoT 6/20, reference-guided 3/20 (Table 4).
bias_by_correction_table.correction_effect_size: CoT reduces math false-accepts 14/20 -> 6/20. Figure 15 shows CoT can still copy a wrong candidate solution. No position-swap delta is reported for CoT.
bias_by_correction_table.locator: Table 4; Figure 15; §3.4 (CoT is for math, not position)
bias_by_correction_table.why_not_measured_effective: Widely copied as 'just add CoT'. Measured effect is math false-accepts, not position bias. Authors show CoT can still be captured by the candidate answers.

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Pairwise LLM judges change winners when candidate order is swapped and systematically prefer a positional slot.
mechanisms.effect_size: GPT-4 Vicuna-13B win rate 51.3% as Assistant 1 vs 23.8% as Assistant 2 on Vicuna-13B vs ChatGPT (conflict 37/80 = 46.3%); GPT-4 MT-Bench consistency 65.0% with 30.0% first-slot bias vs 5.0% second-slot bias (default prompt).
mechanisms.baseline: Unbiased judge: win rate independent of slot (same pair should not flip); consistency 100% on distinguishable pairs. Human majority on the same Vicuna-vs-ChatGPT 80-item set is the alignment baseline in Wang Table 4 (vanilla GPT-4 accuracy 52.7%).
mechanisms.locator: Wang et al. Table 2 and §2.2; Zheng et al. Table 2

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: LLM judges prefer longer/more repetitive answers even when the added text carries no new information, and more than humans do.
mechanisms.effect_size: Repetitive-list attack failure: Claude-v1 91.3%, GPT-3.5 91.3%, GPT-4 8.7% on 23 MT-Bench list answers (Zheng Table 3). Saito accuracy-parity verbosity-bias 0.328 (GPT-4) and 0.428 (GPT-3.5).
mechanisms.baseline: Identical-answer calibration: judges return tie (Zheng §3.3). Parity baseline for Saito's metric is 0 (no verbosity-conditioned accuracy gap). Human preference on HH-RLHF is the alignment baseline in Saito §5.
mechanisms.locator: Zheng et al. Table 3 / §3.3; Saito et al. Table 1

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: A model acting as judge assigns higher win rates or scores to its own generations than humans do, and can recognize its own text.
mechanisms.effect_size: GPT-4 favors itself with a 10% higher win rate vs humans; Claude-v1 25% higher (Zheng Figure 3b / §3.3). GPT-4 out-of-the-box self-recognition 73.5% among itself, two other LLMs, and humans (Panickssery).
mechanisms.baseline: Human win rates on the same model pairs (Zheng Figure 3b). Chance self-recognition among four sources is 25% pairwise-unnormalized; they report >50% for all three models and 73.5% for GPT-4 vs two LLMs + humans.
mechanisms.locator: Zheng et al. Figure 3b and §3.3; Panickssery et al. abstract / §1
mechanisms.caveat: Zheng §3.3 states a controlled self-enhancement study is hard and they cannot determine the cause. Panickssery supplies the recognition correlation; causal self-preference is graded on the +10pp / +25pp vs-human figure, not on a closed intervention.

mechanisms.canonical_mechanism: Judges shift preference toward answers dressed with fake citations (authority) or markdown/emoji 'rich content' (beauty) without a change in semantic quality.
mechanisms.effect_size: Chen Table 1 ASR: GPT-4 fake-reference 0.66 vs random 0.37; rich-content 0.32 vs random 0.39. GPT-4o fake-reference 0.32 (5pp better than random 0.37); rich-content 0.07. Combined authority+beauty attack ASR up to 50% on GPT-4 (abstract / §6).
mechanisms.baseline: Random-judge ASR in the same table (fake-reference 0.37, rich-content 0.39). Control group is the unperturbed answer pair.
mechanisms.locator: Chen et al. Table 1, Take-away 3–4, §6 (50% attack)

declared_schema.note: RES-0001 (shared claim-record family) is not delivered on this worktree. This unit validates against a local schema that enforces the RES-0077 fields (table, grades, sentinel) and rejects garbage documents.

tests.name: grade every correction measured-effective / proposed-only / refuted with a citation
control: at least one widely-cited correction must land outside measured-effective if the evidence says so

reviewer.notes: Two independent reviewers with PARTITIONED evidence: disjoint paper sets. Reviewer A holds Zheng/Wang/Saito/Dubois. Reviewer B holds Panickssery/Chen/Liu. No second same-source reviewer on the same input half.
